newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down on dampened sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down on dampened sentiment.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly lower on Friday due to dampened sentiment following falls in two previous sessions, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 18.92 points or 0.29 percent lower at 6,475.42. Turnover was a modest T$38.88 billion.
Despite ending down, the market showed signs of stabilising after it had lost a total of more than 120 points on Wednesday and Thursday, brokers said.
"Selling pressure has eased somewhat as the market started to find firm support," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming.
"The falls in the previous days were not driven by anything other than pyschological fear, so it is about time the index started to recover," Hou added.
Losses were spread evenly across the sectors -- with plastics dropping 0.61 percent, financials falling 0.31 percent and textiles easing by 0.36 percent.
Electronics outperformed the market to rise 0.24 percent, with Synnex Technology gaining 4.44 percent or T$4 to T$94.

The sector was boosted recently by news that the semiconductor book-to-bill ratio for the United States reached a new year high in September. Investors also expect technology firms to report healthy earning figures for the first three quarters this year.
The deadline for companies to report January-September earning totals is October 31.
Brokers expected the market to remain in a consolidation on Saturday. A 6,450-6,500 range was seen. -- Kevin Chen (5080815)
